advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or defensively enforce) that _previous_canary_red depends on gh api newest-first run ordering, or sort by updated_at before selecting the most recent prior run.
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py:153: `for run in runs if isinstance(runs, list) else []:`
scripts/canary_bridge.py:156-158: returns True/False on the first non-current run — i.e. treats element order as recency order
The gh api query `runs?status=completed&per_page=5` has no explicit sort parameter; correctness depends on GitHub's default created-descending ordering.
advisory.finding: _previous_canary_red relies on the gh api returning workflow runs in newest-first order and returns on the first non-current completed run it encounters; this ordering assumption is implicit and undocumented. If the API ever returns runs unsorted, the threshold could be met/missed against the wrong run.
scenarios: GitHub Actions API returns completed runs in a non-recency order for the workflow

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion (in test_conflict_filing_deferred.py or an applier integration test) that the pending directive reaching _file_conflict_bug_ticket carries local_id and jira_key matching the inbound conflict mutation.
evidence: search of test_conflict_filing_deferred.py for `local_id` returns no matches

apply_inbound.py:404-410 builds `pending_bug_ticket = {title, description, parent_id, local_id, jira_key}` — the local_id/jira_key keys are the dedup input asserted nowhere at the producer→filer boundary

conflict_bug_filing.file_conflict_bug_ticket derives its dedup tag via `conflict_dedup_tag(local_id, jira_key)`; a directive missing those keys degrades every filing to '' identifiers and defeats dedup
advisory.finding: The seam signature was widened to (cli_path, pending) specifically so the conflict filer sees local_id/jira_key for its per-pair dedup tag, but no test asserts the pending directive delivered by applier.apply() actually carries local_id/jira_key. The conflict_bug_filing unit tests build their own _pending() dicts (always with those keys), and the deferred-filing integration tests only capture/assert title/description/parent_id. If _apply_inbound_conflict stopped populating local_id/jira_key in pending_bug_ticket, dedup would silently break (a duplicate ticket every reconciler pass) and every test would still pass.
scenarios: A future refactor of _apply_inbound_conflict drops local_id/jira_key from the pending directive; dedup silently regresses to one ticket per pass; tests stay green
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_apply_files_pending_bug_tickets_after_apply_batch_returns, capture `pending.get("local_id")` and `pending.get("jira_key")` and assert they equal `local-101` / `DIG-101`.
